technical_errors: HIGH CONFIDENCE (~90). Line 281's `cex` enum (`real-bug | spurious-environment | property-bug | abstraction-artifact | not-analysed`) has no value for step 3's third classification bullet, "An initial-state artifact" (lines 150-153). Step 3 sets up exactly four named triage classes — property bug, abstraction artifact, initial-state artifact, spurious input sequence — plus a residual real bug, i.e. five distinct outcomes, but the `cex` field only carries five tokens and none of them is 'initial-state' anything. An engineer who correctly triages a trace that starts in an unreachable initial state (the explicit cycle-0/cycle-1 heuristic the skill itself gives) has no correct token to write in the handoff block and must either invent an unregistered value or mis-file it under `not-analysed` or `spurious-environment` — exactly the kind of drift `_shared/handoff-vocabulary.md` exists to prevent. This is a schema gap distinct from, and more serious than, the confirmed C005 dead-value findings.

HIGH CONFIDENCE (~85). Line 282, inside the handoff-block template: `signature  : phase-kind-where-what per the shared schema, for a real-bug cex only`. The shared schema (`_shared/failure-signature-schema.md`, 'Shape' section) mandates the pipe-delimited form `<phase>|<kind>|<where>|<what>` and states signatures 'are compared exactly. Do not paraphrase.' The sibling golden skill dv-ral-bringup gets this right in the equivalent line of its own block: `signature : phase|kind|where|what, per the shared schema`. This skill's block instead spells it with hyphens, which — if copied literally as the field-order example, the same way the pipe form is copied literally elsewhere in the pack — produces a signature string in the wrong delimiter and breaks the exact-match join the schema exists for.

MODERATE-HIGH CONFIDENCE (~80). Line 284's `vacuity` field offers three values (`clean | suspect | not-checked`), but step 5 (lines 193-214) only ever instructs when to write the equivalent of `clean` (implicitly, when the tool confirms reachability) or `not-checked` (explicitly: 'say the vacuity line is unchecked rather than assuming it is clean'). No sentence anywhere ties a specific reachability/vacuity-check outcome to `suspect`. The only place the word 'suspect' appears in the body is line 211, 'To settle a suspect assumption...', which is about a *convenience assumption under question in the assumption ledger* (step 4), a different axis entirely from the vacuity-check verdict on an antecedent. Because the word 'suspect' does appear verbatim in the prose, a naive text-match dead-value checker (the kind that produced the confirmed C005 findings) would likely pass this field even though no step actually tells the reader when to assign it — this is effectively a sixth dead handoff value that the given C005 list missed.
verb_honesty: No violations found. Every step is framed as Read/Grep/Glob, classification, drafting, or an explicit human handoff. Step 5 correctly hands off re-proving to a person: "ask the formal owner to re-prove the property with that one assumption removed and to give you the path of the new report, then repeat step 2 against it" (line ~212-214). Step 8 is explicit about the write-access boundary: "The agent has no write access to the coverage flow by design: hand the drafted text to the owner ... and ask them to place it" (line 266-267), and the credit entry is explicitly drafted, not placed ("Then draft — do not place — the credit entry", line 264). Step 1's Glob/Glob and steps 2-8's Grep/Read calls are all locate-and-read verbs, never 'run', 'prove', 'merge' or 'submit' applied to the agent. This is one of the stronger parts of the skill.
hallucination_risks: None found at high confidence. Every proprietary fact (report status strings, reachability/vacuity check strings, abstraction pragma names, credit-file format, interface-contract location) is correctly routed through a [[FILL:]] slot rather than invented. The only unmarked specifics are generic IEEE-1800 SVA vocabulary ('assume property', 'cover property', 'cutpoint', 'blackbox') and standard formal-verification concepts (contradiction/dead-end/vacuity, cone of influence, assume-guarantee) that are domain-general rather than house convention, consistent with how the pack's other golden files (e.g. UVM_ERROR/UVM_FATAL in dv-sim-log-first-error) leave standard-language tokens unmarked.
budget_violations: No hard cap violations: the Grep accounting in retrieval-budget point 3 sums exactly to the stated 'at most 9 Greps' (1 in step 2, 2 in step 3, 2 in step 4, 1 in step 5, 1 in step 6, 1 in step 7, 1 conditional in step 8), and the Read accounting sums exactly to the stated 'at most 6 windowed Reads' across steps 2-5.

MODERATE CONFIDENCE (~55-60, included for completeness though below the usual reporting bar). The retrieval-budget's own size description is internally inconsistent: point 3 says the ledger is '6 windowed Reads of about 60 lines, plus one spare 40-line window' and then lists 'the failing property's declaration' as one of the six ~60-line reads — but step 3's procedure text explicitly makes that same read a '40-line Read at its declaration' (line 135), i.e. the same size the budget elsewhere reserves uniquely for the spare. Separately, the spare is described as 'usually the script's abstraction section', but no numbered step ever performs that read (step 4's two Read calls are already spent on the two assumption windows) — so the spare's stated typical use never actually happens in the procedure as written.

LOW-MODERATE CONFIDENCE (~50, noted but not asserted as a defect). Step 1 says 'Two Glob calls ... one for the setup or constraint script and the property files, one for the saved report' — combining two of the three FILL-declared paths (script, properties) into a single Glob call. This only works if those two live under a pattern one Glob call can span; the FILL slot itself asks for 'three paths' without guaranteeing they share a directory, so this is a plausible but unverified assumption rather than a clear violation.
review.open_twice: "Mostly yes, on content: the domain reasoning (contradiction vs. dead-end vs. vacuity, the four-way counterexample triage, cone-of-influence vs. proof-dependency, the credit-gating logic in step 8) is technically sound, dense, and matches the voice/rigor of the golden references (dv-ral-bringup, dv-sim-log-first-error), and verb honesty and slot usage are both clean. But the first time an engineer actually tries to fill the handoff block on a real run, they will hit at least one of the three schema gaps above (no cex token for an initial-state artifact, an unreachable 'suspect' vacuity value, and a signature template with the wrong delimiter) — exactly the kind of paper-cut that makes someone stop trusting the report block and fall back to writing prose instead of using the fenced format the rest of the pack depends on for cross-skill matching."

But three defects block it. (A) Step 1 orders "check any revision or date stamp the two carry against each other and stop if they disagree" — step 1 is allocated only two Globs, budget point 3 assigns every Grep and Read to steps 2-8, and no [[FILL:]] slot declares where such a stamp lives; step 5 then depends on that check's outcome. (B) The routing section names none of the four same-role formal siblings and actively mis-routes: it sends property work to dv-protocol-checker-rule, a junior vip-engineer skill about passive simulation-side VIP checkers, when dv-formal-property-authoring is the pack's home for formal properties and is triggered by this exact situation — and step 3 calls cex: property-bug "the most common outcome". dv-formal-apps and dv-formal-property-authoring both route into this skill; it reciprocates to neither, and steps 2 and 7 dead-end where dv-formal-convergence is the answer. (C) The block offers `run id : whatever identifies this formal run for us` with no slot and no step; the skill claims only three profile facts are read, and the sibling dv-formal-convergence establishes that the profile's Run identity is seed-and-test shaped and needs a separate Formal run identity slot, which this skill lacks. A DV engineer would hit B within the first hour.
